escalations.why: The M1 contract types can't be written in their components' types.py under the frozen import-linter layers (CONSTRAINTS Boundaries: runlog -> core only; charts -> runlog, evaluate only; methods -> core, runlog). Conflicts: runlog.RunRecord.config is train.RunConfig and runlog.RunWriter.__init__ takes a train.RunConfig (runlog -> train is upward); runlog.Checkpoint.methods is Mapping[str, methods.MethodConfig] (runlog -> methods is upward, and methods -> runlog already exists, so a cycle); charts.learning_curve takes baselines.BaselineMeans (charts -> baselines not allowed). import-linter counts TYPE_CHECKING imports (no exclude_type_checking_imports), and mypy strict needs the import, so no annotation trick avoids it. Options for the Revise: move RunConfig and MethodConfig (and BaselineMeans) into a lower component such as core (re-exported under their current IDs), or change the dependency rules (runlog above methods and train is impossible without a cycle; charts -> baselines could be added).

rule_for must return SnakeRule(), but the frozen SnakeRule (src/rllab/baselines/snake.py) subclasses the RulePolicy Protocol without defining its 'description' member, so mypy strict rejects 'SnakeRule()' with [abstract] 'Cannot instantiate abstract class SnakeRule with abstract attribute description'. Routing it through a Callable variable doesn't help (mypy narrows it). Fix: the interface gives SnakeRule its description (class attribute holding the SNAKE-07 sentence, or self.description set in __init__), or M1-T13 is ordered after M1-T15 so its __init__ assigns it. Everything else in M1-T13 is done in the worktree: rule_for/baseline_means in means.py and 10 passing unit tests in tests/unit/rllab/test_means.py; mypy is the only gate failure.

M1-T26 is split mode but the EVAL-05 verdict rule has no frozen entry point. The only frozen symbol is evaluate.final_evaluation(runs, out), which plays final checkpoints and both baselines on FINAL_SEEDS, so a test cannot inject TC-20's inputs (run means s1-s5 = 14,13,15,12,9, rule mean 10, random mean 1, both nulls rejected) or the 3-run case. Freeze a pure verdict seam in evaluate, for example verdict(run_means: Mapping[str, float], rule_mean: float, comparisons: Sequence[Comparison], direction: Literal['higher','lower']) -> Verdict, plus a summary-assembly step that produces learned_mean/learned_range, with a sample, so the tester can write TC-20 and the 3-run bullet against it. Alternatively make M1-T26 solo mode.

M1-T28 Writes is only src/rllab/charts/check.py, but TC-15 calls learning_curve in src/rllab/charts/curve.py (M1-T16's file), which must call the new check and add the under-3-runs band note; nothing imports check.py and the guard blocks curve.py (charts/__init__.py is frozen too). Fix: add src/rllab/charts/curve.py (and tests/unit/rllab/test_check.py for unit tests) to M1-T28's Writes. check.py already holds check_same_settings(runs) raising MixedRunsError naming each RunConfig field other than name/seed that differs.

tests/intent/rllab/test_style.py cannot be made green within M1-T29's Writes (src/rllab/charts/style.py only): nothing imports charts.style, and both red tests need curve.py changes. test_axes_and_title_are_labelled reads ax.get_title() (centre only) but curve.py sets the title with loc='left'; test_lines_are_thin_with_round_caps_and_joins needs solid_capstyle/joinstyle='round' on the lines curve.py draws. Fix: add src/rllab/charts/curve.py to M1-T29 Writes (so curve applies style.py), or have the title test also accept ax.get_title(loc='left').
